description: Indigenous peoples, individuals, titles, and collective terms in the Virginia Company records (c. 1606-1626). 'seeds' are known spellings; the finder also accepts close OCR/early-modern variants for review. 'homonym' marks names shared with a river, an English settlement or shire, or a person, so a bare singular form is ambiguous; plural forms, 'King/weroance of X', and 'X Indians' read as the people. 'plural_only' groups are read as the people only in plural form (singular is the English settlement/shire/bay). 'exact_only' names are short or English-looking, so no fuzzy matching. 'rejected_spellings' never match (reviewer rejections).

IG-001.name: Powhatan
IG-001.homonym: person (Wahunsenacawh, the paramount chief) and town
IG-001.basis: The paramount chiefdom of Tidewater Virginia (Tsenacomoco); also the title of its chief.

IG-002.name: Tanx Powhatan
IG-002.basis: 'Little Powhatan', the town near the falls of the James, attacked in the 1622-23 reprisals.

IG-003.name: Pamunkey
IG-003.basis: Core Powhatan chiefdom on the Pamunkey River; Opechancanough's people.

IG-004.name: Chickahominy
IG-004.basis: Autonomous people allied with the English by the 1614 treaty; on the Chickahominy River.

IG-005.name: Weyanoke
IG-005.basis: Powhatan people on the south side of the upper James; their lands were granted to Sir George Yeardley.

IG-006.name: Paspahegh
IG-006.basis: Powhatan people on whose land Jamestown stood; destroyed in 1610 but the name persisted for the territory.

IG-007.name: Kecoughtan
IG-007.basis: Native town seized in 1610; singular 'Kecoughtan/Kiccowtan' in these records is the English settlement, so only plural forms are read as the people.

IG-008.name: Appamattuck
IG-008.basis: Powhatan people at the mouth of the Appomattox.

IG-009.name: Arrohateck
IG-009.basis: Powhatan people on the James below the falls.

IG-010.name: Quiyoughcohannock
IG-010.basis: Powhatan people on the south side of the James opposite Jamestown.

IG-011.name: Warraskoyack
IG-011.basis: Powhatan people of the lower James; singular forms in these records mostly name the English shire, so only plural forms are read as the people.

IG-012.name: Nansemond
IG-012.basis: People on the Nansemond River, south of Hampton Roads.

IG-013.name: Chesapeake
IG-013.basis: People at the mouth of the Bay; only plural/people forms are read as the people.

IG-014.name: Accomac
IG-014.basis: Eastern Shore people under the 'Laughing King'; singular forms are usually the English shire.

IG-016.name: Patawomeck
IG-016.basis: People on the Potomac; Japazaws's people, where Pocahontas was taken in 1613; trading partners in the 1620s.

IG-018.name: Chiskiack
IG-018.basis: Powhatan people on the York River. 'Chescack/Cheseack' in the plan for a pale between Martin's Hundred and Chiskiack across the peninsula.

IG-019.name: Youghtanund
IG-019.basis: Powhatan people on the upper Pamunkey.

IG-020.name: Monacan
IG-020.basis: Siouan people above the falls of the James; enemies of the Powhatans.

IG-021.name: Mannahoac
IG-021.basis: Siouan people of the northern Piedmont.

IG-022.name: Massawomeck
IG-022.basis: Northern people raiding the Chesapeake; identity debated.

IG-023.name: Susquehannock
IG-023.basis: Iroquoian people at the head of the Bay.

IG-024.name: Piscataway
IG-024.basis: Algonquian people on the north side of the Potomac.

IG-025.name: Nacotchtank
IG-025.basis: Potomac people (Anacostans) who killed Henry Spelman in 1623.

IG-026.name: Chowanoke
IG-026.basis: Algonquian people of the Chowan River; plural forms only (the river is a place).

IP-001.name: Wahunsenacawh (Powhatan)
IP-001.basis: Paramount chief known to the English as Powhatan; father of Pocahontas.

IP-002.name: Opechancanough
IP-002.role: paramount chief after c. 1618; led the 1622 and 1644 attacks
IP-002.basis: Weroance of Pamunkey, later paramount chief; took the name Mangopeesomon in 1621. 'Brother of Powhatan' is not used as a seed: Opitchapam was also Powhatan's brother, and the records name him that way (V03-P0600, 'his Brother Apochankano now Mangopeesomon').

IP-005.name: Nemattanew (Jack of the Feathers)
IP-005.basis: Warrior whose killing preceded the 1622 attack.

IP-006.name: Chanco
IP-006.basis: Christianized Powhatan youth credited with warning Richard Pace. Waterhouse's 1622 relation calls him 'Perries Indian' (servant of William Perry; V03-P0567); the 1623 letter names him 'Chauco' (V04-P0100).

IP-007.name: Japazaws
IP-007.basis: Patawomeck leader involved in the 1613 capture of Pocahontas.

IP-008.name: Namontack
IP-008.basis: Powhatan envoy taken to England in 1608. No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

IP-010.name: Esmy Shichans (Laughing King of Accomac)
IP-010.basis: Eastern Shore weroance who granted land to the English.

IP-012.name: Kemps
IP-012.basis: Powhatan man held at Jamestown in 1609-10. Short and English-looking: exact seed only.

IP-013.name: Comahum
IP-013.role: taken in 1623; named as an actor in the attack at Martin's Hundred
IP-013.basis: Council in Virginia to the Company, April 1623 (V04-P0100): 'The other (called Comahum) an Actor in the Massacre at Martins Hundred ... Wee putt in Chaines'.

IP-014.name: Two Indian maids (Mary and Elizabeth?)
IP-014.role: two Powhatan women in London, sent to the Somers Isles 1621
IP-014.basis: Court Book: committee for 'the two Virginia maydes' in the custody of William Webb (15 Nov 1620, V01-P0227); ordered sent to the Summer Islands 'towards their preferment in marriage' (11 and 13 June 1621, V01-P0289, V01-P0300). The records here do not give their names; 'Mary and Elizabeth' comes from outside these volumes.

IP-015.name: Thomas Rolfe
IP-015.role: son of Pocahontas and John Rolfe, b. 1615
IP-015.basis: Company to the Governor and Council, 1622 (V02-P0048): Opechancanough and the Natives 'haue giuen their Country to m' Rolfes Child ... till he comes of yeares'.

IP-016.name: Indian boy brought by William Perry (1624)
IP-016.role: brought to London 1624; placed with Patrick Copland
IP-016.basis: Court Book 26 April 1624 (V02-P0555): 'an Indian Boy by one William Perry lately come ouer from Virginia'; 28 April 1624 (V02-P0561): the Court entreats 'm' Copeland a Mynister' to take him into his care. Both entries are the same boy. Whether he is Chanco ('Perries Indian' in 1622) is not stated in the records.

IP-017.name: Georgius Thorpe (homo Virginiae)
IP-017.role: Virginian baptized with George Thorpe's name
IP-017.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words. Not to be confused with the Englishman George Thorpe (people dictionary), who is named often.

IP-018.name: Eiakintomino
IP-018.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

IP-019.name: Matahan
IP-019.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

IP-020.name: Machumps
IP-020.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

IP-021.name: Nanawack
IP-021.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

IP-022.name: Totakins
IP-022.basis: No matches in the four volumes (searched 2026-11-01, OCR-tolerant); kept exact-only so it cannot fuzzy-match other words.

Indians.basis: Most common English term. Excludes East/West Indies and 'Indian corne/wheat'.

savages.basis: Pejorative English term for Native people (noun use).

infidels.basis: Religious term; in these records it nearly always means the Natives.

natives.basis: Used for Native people, but also 'natives of England'; excluded when followed by 'of England/this kingdom'.

barbarians.basis: Pejorative noun; the adjective 'barbarous' is not counted.

country people.basis: Can mean Natives or the English colonists; flagged for review.
